title: Nebraska: Sea of Red
description: From Bugeaters to a stadium that becomes a city—then the mountain-west hire who made Saturdays holy.
imageHint: A sea of red on game day in Lincoln

questions.question: Nebraska's football team once played as the Bugeaters—what nickname do they go by today?
questions.explanation: Lincoln sportswriter Cy Sherman tired of "Bugeaters" and borrowed a name sometimes pinned on Iowa. The 1900 team was first to wear it; the state adopted it in 1945.

questions.question: On Cornhuskers game days, which Lincoln venue becomes, by crowd size, Nebraska's "third-largest city"?
questions.explanation: Dedicated in 1923 to Nebraskans who served in the nation's wars. In 2023 a volleyball match drew 92,003 there—the largest crowd ever for a women's sporting event in the U.S.

questions.question: Memorial Stadium's NCAA-record consecutive sellout streak began on Nov. 3 against Missouri—in what year?
questions.explanation: Attendance that day: 36,501. Sellout No. 400 landed in 2024—an overtime loss to Illinois—and the streak is still more than double any other school's.

questions.question: That 1962 sellout era was just starting when Nebraska hired Bob Devaney away from which mountain-west program?
questions.explanation: Devaney arrived for the 1962 season and went 9-2. Within a decade he'd turn a sleepy program into a national power—and hand the keys to his assistant, Tom Osborne.

questions.question: Devaney, hired from Wyoming, won his first national championship for Nebraska in which season?
questions.explanation: They finished it off by beating LSU in the Orange Bowl on Jan. 1, 1971. He won again in 1971, then stepped aside so Osborne could begin the longest assistant-to-throne handoff in college football lore.

deeperMode.title: Deeper: Tunnel and Stone
deeperMode.description: For anyone who has shivered through a November Tunnel Walk

questions.question: Nebraska players take the field to which Alan Parsons Project instrumental—the heartbeat of the Tunnel Walk?
acceptedAnswers: sirius by the alan parsons project
questions.hint: Same track the Bulls made famous in Chicago

questions.question: Carved into Memorial Stadium's southwest corner: "Not the victory but the action; Not the goal but the game; In the deed the glory." Which Nebraska philosophy professor wrote those lines?
questions.hint: He also helped design inscriptions for the Nebraska State Capitol

easterEgg.title: Not the victory but the action
easterEgg.text: Hartley Burr Alexander's lines are carved into the stadium stone. Locals can quote them after a loss. Visitors learn them the hard way.
